name: Knowledge Corpus Curator
description: Review uploaded knowledge-source files for duplication, redundancy, staleness, overlap, and potentially conflicting guidance, then produce an evidence-based curation backlog.
author: Doug Bellingeri
coverImageAlt: Blank documents pass through a central sorting sieve into four organized stacks and one orange review item.
coverImagePrompt:
Use case: stylized-concept
Asset type: AI.Tedt.org skill gallery cover
Primary request: a purposeful visual metaphor for curating a knowledge corpus: a central collection of mixed paper documents passes through a precise circular sorting sieve and resolves into a few orderly evidence groups for human review
Scene/backdrop: an uncluttered warm-paper field with one compact slate sorting platform and no side storage, stationery, or room props
Subject: one central circular sorting sieve holding a small group of completely blank document forms, resolving into four compact blank stacks and one orange outlier represented only through shape, spacing, and material differences
Style/medium: premium editorial illustration with tactile dimensional detail
Composition/framing: exact 16:10 landscape; strong central silhouette and simple forms legible at small card size; scale the complete sieve, every blank document, all five result groups, platform, and shadows into the central 68% of the frame; leave at least 16% calm empty border on all four sides; no object may enter the outer 12%
Lighting/mood: calm, analytical, evidence-led, quietly technical, with restrained cyan backlighting and a sparing orange accent on the isolated review item
Color palette: warm paper #F8F6F0, slate #101820, navy #00446F, cyan #00A9E0, sparing orange #E86027
Constraints: all document surfaces completely blank; no ruled lines, grids, tables, forms, holes, pseudo-writing, text, letters, numbers, interface labels, icons, symbols, logos, trademarks, or watermark; no paw imagery or paw logo; no cats or cat silhouettes; no product UI or Microsoft Fluent branding
